record.original_question: Let ideal semantics define an ideal set as an admissible set of arguments that is contained in every preferred extension, and let the ideal extension be the inclusion-maximal ideal set. Determine the exact computational complexity of credulous acceptance for ideal semantics: given an argumentation framework F=(A,R) and an argument a in A, decide whether a is contained in the ideal extension of F. Resolve the associated exact complexities of ideal-extension non-emptiness and ideal-extension verification when those classifications depend on the credulous-acceptance problem.

evidence.quote: What is the precise computational complexity of credulous acceptance with respect to ideal semantics?
CAI Given F = (A, R) and a ∈ A, is a contained in the ideal extension of F ?
Thus many of the open problems rest on resolving whether CAI is NP-hard or CAI is in coNP.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let an argumentation framework be a pair F = (A, R), where A is a finite set of arguments and R ⊆ A × A is an attack relation. For S ⊆ A and a, b ∈ A, say that S attacks b if (a, b) ∈ R for some a ∈ S, and that S defends an argument c if every argument that attacks c is itself attacked by S. A set S ⊆ A is conflict-free if there are no a, b ∈ S with (a, b) ∈ R, and admissible if it is conflict-free and defends each of its elements. A preferred extension of F is an inclusion-maximal admissible set. An ideal set of F is an admissible set that is contained in every preferred extension of F; the ideal extension of F is the (unique) inclusion-maximal ideal set.

Define the following decision problems:
 (i) CA_I (credulous acceptance under ideal semantics): given F = (A, R) and a ∈ A, decide whether a belongs to the ideal extension of F.
 (ii) NE_I (non-emptiness): given F, decide whether the ideal extension of F is non-empty.
 (iii) VER_I (verification): given F and S ⊆ A, decide whether S is the ideal extension of F.

Determine the exact computational complexity (with respect to polynomial-time many-one reductions) of CA_I, and consequently of NE_I and VER_I, in particular settling whether CA_I is NP-hard or lies in coNP.
artifact.status_search_result: Dunne's work on the computational complexity of ideal semantics established that the principal reasoning problems for ideal semantics in abstract argumentation frameworks are complete for the class Θ₂^P = P^{NP}_{||} (polynomial-time with non-adaptive NP-oracle queries). This resolves the exact complexity of credulous acceptance under ideal semantics (and hence the related non-emptiness and verification problems), placing them strictly between NP/coNP and Π₂^P (assuming standard complexity-class separations).

status_evidence.title: The computational complexity of ideal semantics (Dunne)
status_evidence.snippet: Problems in ideal argumentation are complete for the class P^{NP}_{||} of languages decidable by polynomial time algorithms allowed to make non-adaptive queries to an NP oracle.
status_evidence.claim: Credulous acceptance for ideal semantics in AFs is Θ₂^P-complete (P^{NP}_{||}-complete).

status_evidence.title: The Computational Complexity of Ideal Semantics I: Abstract Argumentation Frameworks
status_evidence.snippet: The natural decision problems arising with the ideal semantics can be decided more efficiently than sceptical admissibility semantics; typical problems are complete for P^{NP}_{||}.
status_evidence.claim: Exact complexity of ideal-semantics decision problems for AFs is settled at Θ₂^P-complete.
